summary: The provider must draw up a written machine-readable, physical or electronically signed EU declaration of conformity for each high-risk AI system, keep it for 10 years, and submit a copy on request.
quote: "The provider shall draw up a written machine readable, physical or electronically signed EU declaration of conformity for each high-risk AI system, and keep it at the disposal of the national competent authorities for 10 years after the high-risk AI system has been placed on the market or put into service. legal_practice_note: Medium for legal-AI vendors whose systems fall within Annex III justice or other high-risk categories; indirect for deployers.

summary: The Commission may adopt delegated acts updating Annex V declaration content when technical progress makes new elements necessary.

summary: The CE marking for high-risk AI systems is subject to Article 30 of Regulation (EC) No 765/2008 general principles.

legal_practice_note: Medium for legal-AI vendors whose systems fall within Annex III justice or other high-risk categories; indirect for deployers.

summary: For digitally provided high-risk AI systems, a digital CE marking may be used only if easily accessible through the system interface or another machine-readable or electronic means.
quote: "For high-risk AI systems provided digitally, a digital CE marking shall be used, only if it can easily be accessed via the interface from which that system is accessed or via an easily accessible machine-readable code or other electronic means."
legal_practice_note: Medium for legal-AI vendors whose systems fall within Annex III justice or other high-risk categories; indirect for deployers.

summary: The CE marking must be visibly, legibly and indelibly affixed to the high-risk AI system, or where appropriate to packaging or accompanying documentation.
quote: "The CE marking shall be affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly for high-risk AI systems. Where that is not possible or not warranted on account of the nature of the high-risk AI system, it shall be affixed to the packaging or to the accompanying documentation, as appropriate."
legal_practice_note: Medium for legal-AI vendors whose systems fall within Annex III justice or other high-risk categories; indirect for deployers.

summary: Where applicable, the CE marking must be followed by the notified body identification number, and that number must also appear in promotional material mentioning CE marking compliance.
quote: "Where applicable, the CE marking shall be followed by the identification number of the notified body responsible for the conformity assessment procedures set out in Article 43. legal_practice_note: Medium for legal-AI vendors whose systems fall within Annex III justice or other high-risk categories; indirect for deployers.

summary: Where other Union law also requires CE marking, the marking must indicate that the high-risk AI system also fulfils that other law.
quote: "Where high-risk AI systems are subject to other Union law which also provides for the affixing of the CE marking, the CE marking shall indicate that the high-risk AI system also fulfil the requirements of that other law."
transitional_note: For high-risk AI systems that become high-risk through Art. 6(1) (Annex I products), corresponding obligations apply from 2027-08-02 under Art. 113(c).
legal_practice_note: Medium for legal-AI vendors whose systems fall within Annex III justice or other high-risk categories; indirect for deployers.

summary: Before placing on the market or putting into service most Annex III high-risk AI systems, the provider or authorised representative must register itself and the system in the Article 71 EU database.

legal_practice_note: Medium for legal-AI vendors whose systems fall in Annex III, including administration-of-justice systems.

summary: Before placing on the market or putting into service an AI system the provider has concluded is not high-risk under Article 6(3), the provider or authorised representative must register itself and the system in the EU database.

transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Medium for legal-AI vendors relying on an Article 6(3) non-high-risk conclusion.

summary: Before putting into service or using most Annex III high-risk AI systems, public-authority and Union-institution deployers, or persons acting on their behalf, must register themselves, select the system, and register its use in the EU database.

quote: "shall include only the following information, as applicable, referred to in:"

Art. 111(2) gives certain existing public-authority high-risk systems until 2030-08-02.
legal_practice_note: Limits the registration information visible for sensitive public-sector systems with indirect legal-practice relevance.

summary: Registrations for Annex III points 1, 6 and 7 high-risk systems in law enforcement, migration, asylum and border-control areas must be made in the secure non-public section of the EU database.
quote: "For high-risk AI systems referred to in points 1, 6 and 7 of Annex III, in the areas of law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control management, the registration referred to in paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 of this Article shall be in a secure non-public section"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite. Art. 111(2) gives certain existing public-authority high-risk systems until 2030-08-02.
legal_practice_note: Mostly indirect for legal practice except public-sector legal or enforcement bodies using these systems.

summary: Annex III point 2 high-risk AI systems must be registered at national level rather than through the main EU-database route.
quote: "High-risk AI systems referred to in point 2 of Annex III shall be registered at national level"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Medium for legal-AI vendors or public bodies if their AI system falls under Annex III point 2.

summary: Providers must design and develop AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons so those persons are informed they are interacting with AI, unless obvious or covered by the specified law-enforcement exception.
quote: "Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed in such a way that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system"
legal_practice_note: High for legal-AI chatbots, intake assistants, and advice tools that interact directly with clients, witnesses, employees, or the public.

summary: Providers of AI systems, including GPAI systems, that generate synthetic audio, image, video or text content must mark outputs in machine-readable and detectable form, subject to the stated assistive-function and law-enforcement exceptions.
quote: "Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content, shall ensure that the outputs of the AI system are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated"

summary: Deployers of emotion-recognition or biometric-categorisation systems must inform exposed natural persons of the system operation and process personal data under applicable EU data-protection law, except for the stated law-enforcement use.
quote: "Deployers of an emotion recognition system or a biometric categorisation system shall inform the natural persons exposed thereto of the operation of the system"
legal_practice_note: Potentially relevant to legal employers, courts, or public bodies if they deploy emotion-recognition or biometric categorisation tools.

summary: Deployers of AI systems that generate or manipulate image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake must disclose that the content was artificially generated or manipulated, subject to law-enforcement and expressive-work limits.
quote: "Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake, shall disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated"
legal_practice_note: High for law firms, legal departments, courts, or legal-AI vendors publishing AI-generated public-facing audiovisual content.

summary: Information required by Article 50(1) to (4) must be given clearly and distinguishably by the first interaction or exposure and must meet applicable accessibility requirements.
quote: "The information referred to in paragraphs 1 to 4 shall be provided to the natural persons concerned in a clear and distinguishable manner at the latest at the time of the first interaction or exposure"
legal_practice_note: High because legal-AI notices to clients, consumers, employees, or the public must be timely, clear, and accessible.

summary: Article 50 transparency obligations do not affect Chapter III high-risk requirements and do not displace other Union or national transparency obligations for AI deployers.
quote: "Paragraphs 1 to 4 shall not affect the requirements and obligations set out in Chapter III, and shall be without prejudice to other transparency obligations laid down in Union or national law for deployers of AI systems"
legal_practice_note: Clarifies that legal AI may have overlapping high-risk and sectoral transparency duties.

summary: The Commission must encourage and facilitate Union-level codes of practice for detecting, marking and labelling artificially generated or manipulated content and may adopt common implementation rules if codes are inadequate.
quote: "The Commission shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level to facilitate the effective implementation of the obligations regarding the detection, marking and labelling of artificially generated or manipulated content"
legal_practice_note: Institutional support for transparency rules that legal-AI providers and deployers may follow.

summary: A general-purpose AI model is classified as systemic-risk when it has high-impact capabilities or Commission-designated equivalent capabilities or impact, with a FLOP-based presumption for high-impact capabilities.

legal_practice_note: Medium for vendors building legal-AI products on foundation models or providing general-purpose AI models.

summary: Annex XIII lists criteria the Commission must consider when determining GPAI models have capabilities or impact equivalent to high-impact capabilities under Article 51.
quote: "the Commission shall take into account the following criteria"
legal_practice_note: Systemic-risk classification can affect GPAI models used in legal AI products.

summary: The Commission must adopt delegated acts to amend systemic-risk thresholds and supplement benchmarks and indicators as needed to reflect technological developments and the state of the art.
quote: "The Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97 to amend the thresholds listed in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article, as well as to supplement benchmarks and indicators in light of evolving technological developments, such as algorithmic improvements or increased hardware efficiency, when necessary, for these thresholds to"
legal_practice_note: Institutional governance mechanics; indirect relevance to legal practices through oversight and guidance.

summary: If the Commission becomes aware of an unnotified GPAI model presenting systemic risks, it may designate the model as one with systemic risk.
quote: "If the Commission becomes aware of a general-purpose AI model presenting systemic risks of which it has not been notified, it may decide to designate it as a model with systemic risk"
legal_practice_note: Commission classification power indirectly affects legal-AI products built on systemic GPAI models.

summary: A provider whose GPAI model meets the Article 51(1)(a) systemic-risk condition must notify the Commission without delay and within two weeks, including information demonstrating that the condition is met.
quote: "the relevant provider shall notify the Commission without delay and in any event within two weeks after that requirement is met or it becomes known that it will be met"
transitional_note: Under Art. 111(3), providers of general-purpose AI models placed on the market before 2025-08-02 must take the necessary steps to comply with Chapter V obligations by 2027-08-02.
legal_practice_note: Medium for legal-AI vendors that provide or build on GPAI models approaching systemic-risk thresholds.

summary: A provider of a model meeting the Article 51(1)(a) threshold may submit substantiated arguments with its notification to show the model exceptionally does not present systemic risks.
quote: "may present, with its notification, sufficiently substantiated arguments to demonstrate that, exceptionally, although it meets that requirement, the general-purpose AI model does not present, due to its specific characteristics, systemic risks"
legal_practice_note: Relevant to GPAI vendors contesting systemic-risk classification for models used in legal AI.

summary: If the Commission finds a provider’s Article 52(2) arguments insufficient and the provider cannot demonstrate absence of systemic risk, it must reject the arguments and the model is considered systemic-risk GPAI.
quote: "it shall reject those arguments, and the general-purpose AI model shall be considered to be a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk"
legal_practice_note: Commission classification decision indirectly affects legal-AI vendors using the model.

summary: The Commission may designate a GPAI model as presenting systemic risks on its own initiative or after a qualified alert from the scientific panel, using Annex XIII criteria.
quote: "The Commission may designate a general-purpose AI model as presenting systemic risks, ex officio or following a qualified alert from the scientific panel pursuant to Article 90(1), point (a), on the basis of criteria set out in Annex XIII"
legal_practice_note: Commission systemic-risk designation affects the regulatory status of GPAI models used by legal-AI vendors.

summary: A provider whose GPAI model was designated systemic-risk under Article 52(4) may request reassessment with objective, detailed and new reasons, no earlier than six months after designation or a maintained designation.
quote: "Providers may request reassessment at the earliest six months after the designation decision"
legal_practice_note: Relevant to GPAI vendors seeking removal of systemic-risk classification for models used in legal AI.

summary: The Commission must publish and keep updated a list of GPAI models with systemic risk while protecting intellectual property, confidential business information, and trade secrets.
quote: "The Commission shall ensure that a list of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk is published and shall keep that list up to date"
legal_practice_note: The public list helps legal-AI vendors and deployers identify systemic-risk GPAI models they rely on.

summary: Providers of GPAI models must draw up and keep current technical documentation of the model, including training, testing and evaluation results, with at least Annex XI information for provision to the AI Office and national competent authorities on request.
quote: "draw up and keep up-to-date the technical documentation of the model, including its training and testing process and the results of its evaluation"
transitional_note: Under Art. 111(3), providers of general-purpose AI models placed on the market before 2025-08-02 must take the necessary steps to comply with Chapter V obligations by 2027-08-02.
legal_practice_note: Medium for vendors that provide GPAI models used in legal-AI products.

summary: Providers of GPAI models must draw up, keep current and make available information and documentation for AI-system providers that intend to integrate the model, enabling understanding of capabilities and limitations and regulatory compliance.
quote: "draw up, keep up-to-date and make available information and documentation to providers of AI systems who intend to integrate the general-purpose AI model into their AI systems"
transitional_note: Under Art. 111(3), providers of general-purpose AI models placed on the market before 2025-08-02 must take the necessary steps to comply with Chapter V obligations by 2027-08-02.
legal_practice_note: Medium for GPAI vendors supplying model documentation to downstream legal-AI providers.

summary: Providers of GPAI models must put in place a policy to comply with Union copyright and related-rights law, including identifying and complying with machine-readable rights reservations under Directive (EU) 2019/790.
quote: "put in place a policy to comply with Union law on copyright and related rights, and in particular to identify and comply with, including through state-of-the-art technologies, a reservation of rights"
transitional_note: Under Art. 111(3), providers of general-purpose AI models placed on the market before 2025-08-02 must take the necessary steps to comply with Chapter V obligations by 2027-08-02.
legal_practice_note: Medium for GPAI vendors whose models may be used by legal-AI systems and trained on protected content.

summary: Providers of GPAI models must draw up and make publicly available a sufficiently detailed summary of training content using the AI Office template.
quote: "draw up and make publicly available a sufficiently detailed summary about the content used for training of the general-purpose AI model, according to a template provided by the AI Office"
transitional_note: Under Art. 111(3), providers of general-purpose AI models placed on the market before 2025-08-02 must take the necessary steps to comply with Chapter V obligations by 2027-08-02.
legal_practice_note: Medium for GPAI vendors and downstream legal-AI providers evaluating training-content disclosures.

summary: The Article 53(1)(a) and (b) documentation duties do not apply to qualifying free and open-source AI models with public parameters, weights, architecture and usage information, but the exception does not cover systemic-risk GPAI models.
quote: "This exception shall not apply to general-purpose AI models with systemic risks"
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI vendors relying on open-source GPAI models; systemic-risk models remain covered.

summary: Providers of GPAI models must cooperate as necessary with the Commission and national competent authorities when those authorities exercise their AI Act competences and powers.
quote: "Providers of general-purpose AI models shall cooperate as necessary with the Commission and the national competent authorities in the exercise of their competences and powers pursuant to this Regulation"
transitional_note: Under Art. 111(3), providers of general-purpose AI models placed on the market before 2025-08-02 must take the necessary steps to comply with Chapter V obligations by 2027-08-02.
legal_practice_note: Medium for GPAI vendors active in legal AI when Commission or national authorities request cooperation.

summary: Providers of GPAI models may rely on codes of practice until harmonised standards are published; providers not adhering to an approved code or European harmonised standard must demonstrate alternative adequate compliance means to the Commission.
quote: "Providers of general-purpose AI models who do not adhere to an approved code of practice or do not comply with a European harmonised standard shall demonstrate alternative adequate means of compliance for assessment by the Commission"
transitional_note: Under Art. 111(3), providers of general-purpose AI models placed on the market before 2025-08-02 must take the necessary steps to comply with Chapter V obligations by 2027-08-02.
legal_practice_note: Medium for GPAI vendors choosing compliance routes for models incorporated into legal-AI systems.

summary: The Commission may adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to detail measurement and calculation methodologies that allow comparable and verifiable Annex XI documentation.
quote: "the Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97 to detail measurement and calculation methodologies with a view to allowing for comparable and verifiable documentation"
legal_practice_note: Institutional power indirectly affects GPAI documentation available to legal-AI vendors.

summary: The Commission may adopt delegated acts under Article 97(2) to amend Annexes XI and XII in light of evolving technological developments.
quote: "The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97(2) to amend Annexes XI and XII in light of evolving technological developments"
legal_practice_note: Institutional power indirectly changes GPAI documentation requirements for legal-AI vendors.

summary: Information and documentation obtained under Article 53, including trade secrets, must be treated according to Article 78 confidentiality obligations.
quote: "Any information or documentation obtained pursuant to this Article, including trade secrets, shall be treated in accordance with the confidentiality obligations set out in Article 78"
legal_practice_note: Protects confidential GPAI information that may include legal-AI vendor or model-provider materials.

summary: Before placing a GPAI model on the Union market, a provider established in a third country must appoint an authorised representative in the Union by written mandate.
quote: "Prior to placing a general-purpose AI model on the Union market, providers established in third countries shall, by written mandate, appoint an authorised representative which is established in the Union."
legal_practice_note: Medium for vendors building legal-AI products on foundation models or providing general-purpose AI models.

summary: The provider must enable the authorised representative to perform its mandated tasks, and the mandate must empower the representative to be addressed by the AI Office or competent authorities.
quote: "The provider shall enable its authorised representative to perform the tasks specified in the mandate received from the provider."
legal_practice_note: Medium for vendors building legal-AI products on foundation models or providing general-purpose AI models.

summary: The authorised representative must verify that Annex XI technical documentation is drawn up and obligations are fulfilled, and keep a copy of that documentation and provider contact details for 10 years.
quote: "The authorised representative shall perform the tasks specified in the mandate received from the provider. It shall provide a copy of the mandate to the AI Office upon request, in one of the official languages of the institutions of the Union. For the purposes of this Regulation, the mandate shall empower the"
legal_practice_note: Medium for vendors building legal-AI products on foundation models or providing general-purpose AI models.

summary: The authorised representative must provide the AI Office, on reasoned request, compliance information and documentation and cooperate with the AI Office and competent authorities on GPAI-model actions.
quote: "The authorised representative shall perform the tasks specified in the mandate received from the provider. It shall provide a copy of the mandate to the AI Office upon request, in one of the official languages of the institutions of the Union. For the purposes of this Regulation, the mandate shall empower the"
legal_practice_note: Medium for vendors building legal-AI products on foundation models or providing general-purpose AI models.

summary: The authorised representative must terminate the mandate and immediately inform the AI Office if it considers the provider non-compliant; Article 54 does not apply to qualifying open-source models unless systemic-risk.
quote: "The authorised representative shall terminate the mandate if it considers or has reason to consider the provider to be acting contrary to its obligations pursuant to this Regulation. In such a case, it shall also immediately inform the AI Office about the termination of the mandate and the reasons therefor."
legal_practice_note: Medium for vendors building legal-AI products on foundation models or providing general-purpose AI models.

summary: Providers of GPAI models with systemic risk must perform model evaluation using state-of-the-art standardised protocols and tools, including documented adversarial testing to identify and mitigate systemic risks.
quote: "perform model evaluation in accordance with standardised protocols and tools reflecting the state of the art, including conducting and documenting adversarial testing of the model with a view to identifying and mitigating systemic risks;"
legal_practice_note: Medium for vendors building legal-AI products on foundation models or providing general-purpose AI models.

summary: Providers of GPAI models with systemic risk must assess and mitigate possible Union-level systemic risks and their sources from development, market placement or use of the model.
quote: "assess and mitigate possible systemic risks at Union level, including their sources, that may stem from the development, the placing on the market, or the use of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk;"
legal_practice_note: Medium for vendors building legal-AI products on foundation models or providing general-purpose AI models.

summary: Providers of GPAI models with systemic risk must track, document and report serious incidents and possible corrective measures without undue delay to the AI Office and, where appropriate, national competent authorities.
quote: "keep track of, document, and report, without undue delay, to the AI Office and, as appropriate, to national competent authorities, relevant information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures to address them;"
legal_practice_note: Medium for vendors building legal-AI products on foundation models or providing general-purpose AI models.

summary: Providers of GPAI models with systemic risk must ensure adequate cybersecurity protection for the model and its physical infrastructure.
quote: "ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity protection for the general-purpose AI model with systemic risk and the physical infrastructure of the model."
legal_practice_note: Medium for vendors building legal-AI products on foundation models or providing general-purpose AI models.

summary: Providers of systemic-risk GPAI models may rely on codes of practice or harmonised standards to demonstrate compliance, and must demonstrate alternative adequate means if not using them; information obtained is confidential.
quote: "Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk may rely on codes of practice within the meaning of Article 56 to demonstrate compliance with the obligations set out in paragraph 1 of this Article, until a harmonised standard is published. Compliance with European harmonised standards grants providers the presumption of conformity to"
legal_practice_note: Medium for vendors building legal-AI products on foundation models or providing general-purpose AI models.

summary: The AI Office must encourage and facilitate Union-level codes of practice that contribute to proper AI Act application while taking international approaches into account.
quote: "The AI Office shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level in order to contribute to the proper application of this Regulation"
legal_practice_note: Governance row with indirect importance for legal-AI vendors using GPAI models.

summary: The AI Office and Board must aim for codes of practice to cover Articles 53 and 55, including current information, training-content summaries, systemic-risk types, and systemic-risk assessment and management measures.
quote: "The AI Office and the Board shall aim to ensure that the codes of practice cover at least the obligations provided for in Articles 53 and 55"
legal_practice_note: Governance of GPAI compliance tools that downstream legal-AI vendors may rely on.

summary: The AI Office may invite GPAI model providers and relevant national competent authorities to participate in code drafting, with support from civil society, industry, academia and other stakeholders.
quote: "The AI Office may invite all providers of general-purpose AI models, as well as relevant national competent authorities, to participate in the drawing-up of codes of practice"
legal_practice_note: Governance participation route for GPAI vendors, including those serving legal-AI markets.

summary: The AI Office and Board must aim for codes of practice to state specific objectives and contain commitments or measures, including KPIs where appropriate, while considering interested parties and affected persons.
quote: "The AI Office and the Board shall aim to ensure that the codes of practice clearly set out their specific objectives and contain commitments or measures"
legal_practice_note: Indirect governance of the codes that may structure GPAI compliance for legal-AI vendors.

summary: The AI Office must aim for code participants to report regularly on implementation of commitments, measures, outcomes and KPIs, with reporting reflecting participant size and capacity.
quote: "The AI Office shall aim to ensure that participants to the codes of practice report regularly to the AI Office on the implementation of the commitments and the measures taken and their outcomes"
legal_practice_note: Indirect monitoring framework for GPAI providers whose models may support legal AI.

summary: The Commission and Board must monitor and evaluate code objectives and contribution to proper application; the Commission must assess coverage of Articles 53 and 55 and publish its adequacy assessment.
quote: "The Commission and the Board shall regularly monitor and evaluate the achievement of the objectives of the codes of practice by the participants and their contribution to the proper application of this Regulation"
legal_practice_note: Governance assessment that indirectly affects GPAI compliance expectations for legal-AI vendors.

summary: The AI Office may invite all GPAI model providers to adhere to codes of practice, with non-systemic providers limited to Article 53 obligations unless they choose the full code.
quote: "The AI Office may invite all providers of general-purpose AI models to adhere to the codes of practice"
legal_practice_note: Governance invitation relevant to GPAI vendors whose models may be integrated into legal-AI systems.

summary: The AI Office must, where appropriate, encourage and facilitate review and adaptation of codes of practice, especially in light of emerging standards, and assist in assessing available standards.
quote: "The AI Office shall, as appropriate, also encourage and facilitate the review and adaptation of the codes of practice, in particular in light of emerging standards"
legal_practice_note: Indirectly affects updates to GPAI codes used by legal-AI providers.

summary: Codes of practice had to be ready by 2 May 2025, and the AI Office had to take necessary steps, including inviting providers to adhere.
quote: "Codes of practice shall be ready at the latest by 2 May 2025. The AI Office shall take the necessary steps, including inviting providers pursuant to paragraph 7"
legal_practice_note: Governance deadline for GPAI codes that may guide legal-AI vendors.

summary: Member States must ensure their competent authorities establish at least one national AI regulatory sandbox, operational by 2 August 2027; it may be established jointly with other Member States.
quote: "Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities establish at least one AI regulatory sandbox at national level, which shall be operational by 2 August 2027"
applies_from_basis: Art. 57(1) operational deadline as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744
legal_practice_note: Sandbox availability may help legal-AI providers test innovative systems, but this is a Member State infrastructure duty.
applies_from_basis_as_enacted: Art. 113 second subparagraph; Art. 57(1) as enacted required operation by 2 August 2026

summary: The Commission may provide technical support, advice and tools for the establishment and operation of AI regulatory sandboxes.
quote: "The Commission may provide technical support, advice and tools for the establishment and operation of AI regulatory sandboxes"
legal_practice_note: Institutional support with indirect benefit for legal-AI innovators using sandboxes.

summary: Additional AI regulatory sandboxes may be established at regional or local level, or jointly with competent authorities of other Member States.
quote: "Additional AI regulatory sandboxes at regional or local level, or established jointly with the competent authorities of other Member States may also be established"
legal_practice_note: Additional sandbox capacity may indirectly support legal-AI providers.

summary: The European Data Protection Supervisor may establish an AI regulatory sandbox for Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies, with Chapter VI references to national competent authorities construed accordingly.
quote: "The European Data Protection Supervisor may establish an AI regulatory sandbox for Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies"
legal_practice_note: Relevant mainly to EU institutions, with indirect legal-practice relevance for EU public-sector legal functions.

summary: National competent authorities may cooperate with other relevant authorities and involve other AI-ecosystem actors; Member States must ensure cooperation between supervisors of other sandboxes and national competent authorities.
quote: "Member States shall ensure an appropriate level of cooperation between the authorities supervising those other sandboxes and the national competent authorities"
legal_practice_note: Coordination of sandbox authorities indirectly affects legal-AI innovators seeking multi-regime guidance.

summary: Member States must ensure competent authorities allocate sufficient resources to comply with Article 57 effectively and in a timely manner.
quote: "Member States shall ensure that the competent authorities referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 allocate sufficient resources to comply with this Article effectively and in a timely manner"
legal_practice_note: Governance resource duty that indirectly supports sandbox access for legal-AI providers.

summary: AI regulatory sandboxes must provide a controlled environment that supports development, training, testing and validation of innovative AI systems for a limited time before market placement or service, under an agreed plan with safeguards.
quote: "AI regulatory sandboxes established under this Article shall provide for a controlled environment that fosters innovation and facilitates the development, training, testing and validation of innovative AI systems"
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI providers using sandboxes to develop or test innovative legal-sector AI systems.

summary: Where a sandbox includes testing in real world conditions, the sandbox plan must incorporate the real-world testing plan referred to in Articles 60 and 60a where applicable.
quote: "Where applicable, the sandbox plan shall incorporate the real-world testing plan referred to in Articles 60 and 60a"
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI providers conducting sandbox-based real-world testing.

summary: Competent authorities must provide guidance, supervision and support within AI regulatory sandboxes to identify risks, testing, mitigation measures and their effectiveness under the AI Act and other supervised law.
quote: "Competent authorities shall provide, as appropriate, guidance, supervision and support within the AI regulatory sandbox with a view to identifying risks"
legal_practice_note: Sandbox guidance may help legal-AI providers understand regulatory expectations.

summary: Competent authorities must provide participating providers and prospective providers with guidance on regulatory expectations and how to fulfil AI Act requirements and obligations.
quote: "Competent authorities shall provide providers and prospective providers participating in the AI regulatory sandbox with guidance on regulatory expectations and how to fulfil the requirements and obligations set out in this Regulation"
legal_practice_note: Directly useful to legal-AI providers participating in a sandbox.

summary: Subject to confidentiality and provider agreement, the Commission and Board may access sandbox exit reports and consider them when performing AI Act tasks; an exit report may be made public if both provider and authority agree.
quote: "the Commission and the Board shall be authorised to access the exit reports and shall take them into account, as appropriate, when exercising their tasks under this Regulation"
legal_practice_note: Exit reports may inform AI Act governance affecting legal-AI sandbox participants.

summary: AI regulatory sandboxes must aim to improve legal certainty, share best practices, foster innovation and competitiveness, support evidence-based regulatory learning, and facilitate and accelerate Union-market access, especially for SMEs, start-ups and SMCs.
quote: "The establishment of AI regulatory sandboxes shall aim to contribute to the following objectives:"
legal_practice_note: Sandbox objectives may benefit legal-AI SMEs and start-ups but are principally institutional.

summary: National competent authorities must associate data protection authorities and other competent authorities with sandbox operation and supervision when innovative AI systems involve personal-data processing or fall within those authorities’ remits.
quote: "National competent authorities shall ensure that, to the extent the innovative AI systems involve the processing of personal data or otherwise fall under the supervisory remit of other national authorities"
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI sandbox projects processing client, employee, court, or public-sector personal data.

summary: Significant health, safety or fundamental-rights risks identified during sandbox development and testing must be adequately mitigated; national competent authorities may temporarily or permanently suspend testing or participation if effective mitigation is impossible and must inform the AI Office.
quote: "Any significant risks to health and safety and fundamental rights identified during the development and testing of such AI systems shall result in an adequate mitigation"
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI sandbox tests that may affect fundamental rights or access to justice.

summary: Sandbox participants remain liable for third-party damage from experimentation, but no administrative fines are imposed for AI Act infringements when prospective providers follow the plan, participation terms and good-faith authority guidance.
quote: "Providers and prospective providers participating in the AI regulatory sandbox shall remain liable under applicable Union and national liability law for any damage inflicted on third parties"
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI providers experimenting in sandboxes because liability remains despite fine relief.

summary: AI regulatory sandboxes must be designed and implemented so that, where relevant, they facilitate cross-border cooperation between national competent authorities.
quote: "The AI regulatory sandboxes shall be designed and implemented in such a way that, where relevant, they facilitate cross-border cooperation between national competent authorities"
legal_practice_note: Cross-border sandbox cooperation may indirectly help legal-AI providers operating in multiple Member States.

summary: National competent authorities, the EDPS and the AI Office must coordinate and cooperate within the Board framework, and may support joint sandbox establishment, operation and exchange of best practices.
quote: "National competent authorities, the European Data Protection Supervisor and the AI Office, shall, as appropriate and within their respective competences, coordinate their activities and cooperate within the framework of the Board"
legal_practice_note: Institutional coordination may improve sandbox consistency for legal-AI providers.

summary: National competent authorities must inform the AI Office and Board when establishing a sandbox and may ask for support; the AI Office must publish and update a list of planned and existing sandboxes.
quote: "National competent authorities shall inform the AI Office and the Board of the establishment of a sandbox, and may ask them for support and guidance"
legal_practice_note: Public sandbox information helps legal-AI innovators identify available sandboxes.

summary: National competent authorities must submit annual and final sandbox reports to the AI Office and Board, publish the reports or abstracts online, and the Commission must consider them where appropriate when exercising AI Act tasks.
quote: "National competent authorities shall submit annual reports to the AI Office and to the Board, from one year after the establishment of the AI regulatory sandbox and every year thereafter until its termination, and a final report"
legal_practice_note: Sandbox reporting may indirectly surface lessons for legal-AI systems tested in sandboxes.

summary: The Commission must develop a single dedicated interface containing relevant sandbox information so stakeholders can interact with sandboxes, raise enquiries and seek non-binding guidance on conformity of innovative AI-embedded offerings.
quote: "The Commission shall develop a single and dedicated interface containing all relevant information related to AI regulatory sandboxes to allow stakeholders to interact with AI regulatory sandboxes"
legal_practice_note: The interface may help legal-AI providers find sandbox contacts and non-binding conformity guidance.

summary: The AI Office may establish a Union-level AI regulatory sandbox for Article 75(1) systems, in close cooperation with relevant authorities and with priority access for SMEs, start-ups and SMCs.
quote: "The AI Office may establish an AI regulatory sandbox at Union level for AI systems covered by Article 75(1)"
legal_practice_note: Union-level sandbox may indirectly assist legal-AI SMEs and start-ups whose systems fall under Article 75(1).

summary: To avoid Union fragmentation, the Commission must adopt implementing acts specifying detailed arrangements for AI regulatory sandbox establishment, development, implementation, operation, governance and supervision, including common principles.
quote: "the Commission shall adopt implementing acts specifying the detailed arrangements for the establishment, development, implementation, operation, governance, and supervision of the AI regulatory sandboxes"
legal_practice_note: Institutional rules for sandboxes that may be used by legal-AI providers.

summary: The sandbox implementing acts must ensure transparent and fair access, broad and equal participation, flexibility, free SME access subject to limited cost recovery, streamlined procedures, mutual recognition, appropriate duration and testing infrastructure.
quote: "The implementing acts referred to in paragraph 1 shall ensure:"
legal_practice_note: Implementation principles can affect how legal-AI SMEs and providers access sandboxes.

summary: Prospective providers in AI regulatory sandboxes, especially SMEs and start-ups, must be directed where relevant to pre-deployment guidance and other value-adding services such as standardisation, certification, testing facilities, EDIHs and centres of excellence.
quote: "Prospective providers in the AI regulatory sandboxes, in particular SMEs and start-ups, shall be directed, where relevant, to pre-deployment services such as guidance on the implementation of this Regulation"
legal_practice_note: Useful to legal-AI SMEs or start-ups seeking pre-deployment support.

summary: Where appropriate, national competent authorities must cooperate with other national competent authorities to ensure consistent practices for real-world testing supervised in sandboxes across the Union.
quote: "Where appropriate, they shall cooperate with other national competent authorities with a view to ensuring consistent practices across the Union"
legal_practice_note: Consistency of sandbox testing practices indirectly benefits legal-AI providers operating cross-border.

summary: When national competent authorities consider authorising real-world testing supervised in a sandbox, they must specifically agree the testing terms, conditions and appropriate safeguards with participants to protect fundamental rights, health and safety.
quote: "they shall specifically agree the terms and conditions of such testing and, in particular, the appropriate safeguards with the participants, with a view to protecting fundamental rights, health and safety"
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI providers testing systems that may affect rights, clients, court users, or public services.

summary: In an AI regulatory sandbox, personal data lawfully collected for other purposes may be processed only to develop, train and test certain AI systems when all Article 59(1) cumulative conditions are met.
quote: "personal data lawfully collected for other purposes may be processed solely for the purpose of developing, training and testing certain AI systems in the sandbox when all of the following conditions are met"
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI sandbox projects using existing personal data to develop or test AI systems.

summary: The sandbox AI system must be developed to safeguard a substantial public interest by a public authority or another person in one or more listed areas such as public safety, health, environment, energy, transport, critical infrastructure, public administration or public services.
quote: "AI systems shall be developed for safeguarding substantial public interest by a public authority or another natural or legal person and in one or more of the following areas"
legal_practice_note: Usually indirect for legal practice unless a public legal body develops AI for public administration or services.

summary: The personal data processed in the sandbox must be necessary to comply with one or more Chapter III Section 2 requirements that cannot effectively be met with anonymised, synthetic or other non-personal data.
quote: "the data processed are necessary for complying with one or more of the requirements referred to in Chapter III, Section 2 where those requirements cannot effectively be fulfilled by processing anonymised, synthetic or other non-personal data"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant when legal-AI sandbox testing needs real personal data to meet high-risk requirements.

summary: Effective monitoring mechanisms must identify whether high risks to data-subject rights and freedoms arise during sandbox experimentation, with response mechanisms to promptly mitigate risks and stop processing where necessary.
quote: "there are effective monitoring mechanisms to identify if any high risks to the rights and freedoms of the data subjects"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI sandbox projects processing sensitive client, employee, court-user, or public-service personal data.

summary: Personal data processed in a sandbox must be kept in a functionally separate, isolated and protected data-processing environment under the prospective provider’s control, with access limited to authorised persons.
quote: "any personal data to be processed in the context of the sandbox are in a functionally separate, isolated and protected data processing environment under the control of the prospective provider"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI sandbox tests involving confidential or personal legal data.

summary: Providers may further share originally collected personal data only under Union data-protection law, and personal data created in the sandbox may not be shared outside the sandbox.
quote: "providers can further share the originally collected data only in accordance with Union data protection law; any personal data created in the sandbox cannot be shared outside the sandbox"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI providers limiting onward sharing of personal data generated or used during sandbox tests.

summary: Personal-data processing in the sandbox must not lead to measures or decisions affecting data subjects and must not affect their Union data-protection rights.
quote: "any processing of personal data in the context of the sandbox neither leads to measures or decisions affecting the data subjects nor does it affect the application of their rights"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI sandbox projects so experimentation does not determine legal outcomes for data subjects.

summary: Personal data processed in the sandbox must be protected by appropriate technical and organisational measures and deleted once sandbox participation ends or the retention period expires.
quote: "any personal data processed in the context of the sandbox are protected by means of appropriate technical and organisational measures and deleted once the participation in the sandbox has terminated"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to retention and deletion of personal legal data in sandbox projects.

summary: Logs of personal-data processing in the sandbox must be kept for the duration of sandbox participation unless Union or national law provides otherwise.
quote: "the logs of the processing of personal data in the context of the sandbox are kept for the duration of the participation in the sandbox"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to auditability of legal-AI sandbox projects using personal data.

summary: A complete and detailed description of the process and rationale behind the AI system’s training, testing and validation must be kept with testing results as part of Annex IV technical documentation.
quote: "a complete and detailed description of the process and rationale behind the training, testing and validation of the AI system is kept together with the testing results"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to high-risk legal-AI providers creating technical documentation during sandbox development.

summary: A short summary of the sandbox AI project, objectives and expected results must be published on the competent authority’s website, excluding sensitive operational data for law enforcement, border, immigration or asylum authorities.
quote: "a short summary of the AI project developed in the sandbox, its objectives and expected results is published on the website of the competent authorities"
legal_practice_note: Public summaries may describe public-interest legal-AI sandbox projects without sensitive operational data.

summary: For law-enforcement purposes under authority control and responsibility, personal-data processing in AI regulatory sandboxes must be based on specific Union or national law and meet the same cumulative conditions as Article 59(1).
quote: "the processing of personal data in AI regulatory sandboxes shall be based on a specific Union or national law and subject to the same cumulative conditions as referred to in paragraph 1"
legal_practice_note: Relevant mainly to public legal or law-enforcement authorities, not ordinary legal practice.

summary: Article 59(1) does not override Union or national laws excluding further processing or laws providing a separate basis for developing, testing or training innovative AI systems in compliance with EU data-protection law.
quote: "Paragraph 1 is without prejudice to Union or national law which excludes processing of personal data for other purposes than those explicitly mentioned in that law"
legal_practice_note: Clarifies that legal-AI sandbox projects must still respect applicable data-protection and sectoral limits.

summary: Providers or prospective providers may conduct real-world testing of Annex III or Annex I Section A high-risk AI systems outside sandboxes only under Article 60 and the real-world testing plan, without prejudice to Article 5 prohibitions.
quote: "Testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes may be conducted by providers or prospective providers of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III or covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Section A of Annex I"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI providers testing Annex III high-risk systems outside sandboxes.

summary: Providers or prospective providers may conduct pre-market real-world testing of covered high-risk AI systems on their own or with deployers or prospective deployers.
quote: "Providers or prospective providers may conduct testing of high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III or covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Section A of Annex I in real world conditions at any time before the placing on the market"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI providers and participating deployers in pre-market tests of high-risk systems.

summary: Real-world testing under Article 60 does not displace any ethical review required by Union or national law.
quote: "The testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions under this Article shall be without prejudice to any ethical review that is required by Union or national law"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant where legal-AI testing involving people, courts or public services triggers ethical review.

summary: A provider or prospective provider may conduct real-world testing only after drawing up a real-world testing plan and submitting it to the market surveillance authority in the Member State where testing will occur.
quote: "the provider or prospective provider has drawn up a real-world testing plan and submitted it to the market surveillance authority in the Member State where the testing in real world conditions is to be conducted"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI providers planning high-risk real-world tests.

summary: Real-world testing may proceed only when the market surveillance authority approves the testing and plan, or where applicable is deemed to have approved after 30 days; national law may require express authorisation.
quote: "the market surveillance authority in the Member State where the testing in real world conditions is to be conducted has approved the testing in real world conditions and the real-world testing plan"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI providers needing authority approval for high-risk real-world tests.

summary: The provider or prospective provider must register real-world testing with the required Union-wide identification number and information in the appropriate EU database, secure non-public database section, or national register depending on the system category.
quote: "the provider or prospective provider, with the exception of providers or prospective providers of high-risk AI systems referred to in points 1, 6 and 7 of Annex III"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI providers registering high-risk real-world tests.

summary: The provider or prospective provider conducting real-world testing must be established in the Union or have appointed a legal representative established in the Union.
quote: "the provider or prospective provider conducting the testing in real world conditions is established in the Union or has appointed a legal representative who is established in the Union"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to non-EU legal-AI vendors conducting high-risk testing in the Union.

summary: Data collected and processed for real-world testing may be transferred to third countries only when appropriate and applicable Union-law safeguards are implemented.
quote: "data collected and processed for the purpose of the testing in real world conditions shall be transferred to third countries only provided that appropriate and applicable safeguards under Union law are implemented"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI testing involving cross-border processing of personal or confidential data.

summary: Real-world testing must last no longer than necessary and no longer than six months, with one additional six-month extension only after prior notification to the market surveillance authority and an explanation of need.
quote: "the testing in real world conditions does not last longer than necessary to achieve its objectives and in any case not longer than six months"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI providers setting duration for high-risk real-world tests.

summary: Persons belonging to vulnerable groups due to age or disability who are subjects of real-world testing must be appropriately protected.
quote: "the subjects of the testing in real world conditions who are persons belonging to vulnerable groups due to their age or disability, are appropriately protected"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI tests involving children, older persons, or persons with disabilities.

summary: When a provider or prospective provider tests with deployers or prospective deployers, they must inform them of relevant testing aspects, provide Article 13 instructions for use, and conclude an agreement specifying roles and responsibilities for compliance.
quote: "the latter have been informed of all aspects of the testing that are relevant to their decision to participate, and given the relevant instructions for use of the AI system referred to in Article 13"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant when law firms, courts, or legal departments participate as deployers in high-risk tests.

summary: Real-world testing subjects must give informed consent under Article 61, except in the specified law-enforcement case where testing and outcomes must not negatively affect subjects and personal data must be deleted after the test.
quote: "the subjects of the testing in real world conditions have given informed consent in accordance with Article 61"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI providers running tests with clients, employees, court users, or the public.

summary: Real-world testing must be effectively overseen by the provider or prospective provider and by participating deployers or prospective deployers through suitably qualified persons with the necessary capacity, training and authority.
quote: "the testing in real world conditions is effectively overseen by the provider or prospective provider, as well as by deployers or prospective deployers through persons who are suitably qualified"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to law firms, courts, or legal departments participating in supervised high-risk testing.

summary: The predictions, recommendations or decisions of the AI system used in real-world testing must be capable of being effectively reversed and disregarded.
quote: "the predictions, recommendations or decisions of the AI system can be effectively reversed and disregarded"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: High for legal or justice AI tests because AI outputs must not irreversibly determine legal outcomes.

summary: Any real-world testing subject, or legally designated representative, may withdraw at any time without detriment or justification by revoking informed consent and may request immediate and permanent deletion of personal data.
quote: "Any subjects of the testing in real world conditions, or their legally designated representative, as appropriate, may, without any resulting detriment and without having to provide any justification, withdraw from the testing at any time"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to individuals participating in legal-AI or justice-AI real-world tests.

summary: Member States must confer powers on market surveillance authorities to require information, conduct unannounced remote or on-site inspections, and check real-world testing and related high-risk AI systems; authorities must use those powers to ensure safe testing development.
quote: "Member States shall confer on their market surveillance authorities the powers of requiring providers and prospective providers to provide information, of carrying out unannounced remote or on-site inspections"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Enforcement powers may affect legal-AI providers conducting high-risk real-world testing.

summary: After a serious incident in real-world testing, the provider or prospective provider must adopt immediate mitigation measures or suspend testing until mitigation occurs, or otherwise terminate it.
quote: "The provider or prospective provider shall adopt immediate mitigation measures or, failing that, shall suspend the testing in real world conditions until such mitigation takes place, or otherwise terminate it"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI providers managing incidents during high-risk testing.

summary: Upon termination of real-world testing after a serious incident, the provider or prospective provider must have a procedure for promptly recalling the AI system.
quote: "The provider or prospective provider shall establish a procedure for the prompt recall of the AI system upon such termination of the testing in real world conditions"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI providers terminating a high-risk test after an incident.

summary: Any serious incident identified during real-world testing must be reported to the national market surveillance authority in accordance with Article 73.
quote: "Any serious incident identified in the course of the testing in real world conditions shall be reported to the national market surveillance authority in accordance with Article 73"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI providers if high-risk testing causes or reveals serious incidents.

summary: Providers or prospective providers must notify the national market surveillance authority in the testing Member State of suspension or termination of real-world testing and of final outcomes.
quote: "Providers or prospective providers shall notify the national market surveillance authority in the Member State where the testing in real world conditions is to be conducted of the suspension or termination of the testing in real world conditions and of the final outcomes"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI providers closing or suspending high-risk tests.

summary: The provider or prospective provider is liable under applicable Union and national liability law for damage caused during real-world testing.
quote: "The provider or prospective provider shall be liable under applicable Union and national liability law for any damage caused in the course of their testing in real world conditions"
transitional_note: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2027-12-02 for Annex III high-risk systems and 2028-08-02 for Annex I high-risk systems under Art. 113(c) as amended; this row applies when the relevant high-risk rules bite.
legal_practice_note: Relevant to legal-AI providers because liability remains for harms during high-risk tests.

summary: Member States may allow real-world testing outside sandboxes by providers or prospective providers of AI-enabled products covered by Annex I Section B harmonisation legislation to assess and verify conformity with Articles 8 to 15.
quote: "Member States may allow, in accordance with this Article, the testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes by providers or prospective providers of AI enabled products"
legal_practice_note: Mostly indirect for legal practice unless a legal-AI system is part of an Annex I Section B product.

summary: Member States that choose to allow Article 60a testing must, individually or jointly, adopt frameworks for real-world testing.
quote: "Member States that choose to allow testing as referred to in paragraph 1 shall, individually or jointly, adopt frameworks for real-world testing"
legal_practice_note: Framework duty has indirect relevance to legal-AI providers in regulated products.

summary: Each Member State must notify the Commission of any real-world testing framework it adopts before implementing the framework, without affecting Commission competences under Annex I Section B harmonisation legislation.
quote: "Each Member State shall notify the Commission of any real-world testing framework it adopts before implementing it"
legal_practice_note: Institutional notification with indirect legal-practice relevance.

summary: Member States with real-world testing frameworks must ensure relevant competent, relevant and public infrastructure authorities cooperate closely in good faith and remove practical obstacles, including procedural barriers to physical public infrastructure access when necessary.
quote: "shall ensure that the relevant national competent authorities, relevant authorities and public authorities responsible for the management and operation of infrastructure and products covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Section B of Annex I cooperate closely with each other in good faith"
legal_practice_note: Mostly indirect for legal practice unless legal-AI products depend on regulated public infrastructure.

summary: Article 60a frameworks must ensure compliance with listed Article 60 testing safeguards, include effective governance and accountability arrangements, and ensure a high level of health, safety and fundamental-rights protection.
quote: "ensure compliance with the requirements laid down in Article 60(2), (3), (4)(d)-(j) and (5)-(9)"
legal_practice_note: Indirect for legal-AI providers unless they test AI-enabled regulated products under Annex I Section B.

summary: Article 60a real-world testing frameworks must require a mandatory testing plan agreed between the provider or prospective provider and the national competent or relevant authority under Annex I Section B harmonisation legislation.
quote: "include the provision of a mandatory real-world testing plan to be agreed between the provider or prospective provider and the national competent authority or relevant authority"
legal_practice_note: Indirect for legal-AI providers unless they test AI-enabled regulated products.

summary: Real-world testing under Article 60a must comply with applicable provisions of Annex I Section B Union harmonisation legislation, without those provisions preventing Article 60a testing to the extent necessary.
quote: "The real-world testing shall comply with the applicable provisions laid down in the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Section B of Annex I"
legal_practice_note: Indirect for legal-AI providers unless covered by Annex I Section B harmonisation legislation.

summary: For Article 60 real-world testing, freely given informed consent must be obtained before participation after concise, clear, relevant and understandable information on nature, conditions, rights, reversal arrangements and identification/contact details.
quote: "For the purpose of testing in real world conditions under Article 60, freely-given informed consent shall be obtained from the subjects of testing prior to their participation in such testing and after their having been duly informed with concise, clear, relevant, and understandable information regarding:"
legal_practice_note: Medium for legal-AI vendors testing high-risk systems with natural-person subjects.

summary: Informed consent for Article 60 real-world testing must be dated and documented, and a copy must be given to the test subject or legal representative.
quote: "The informed consent shall be dated and documented and a copy shall be given to the subjects of testing or their legal representative."
legal_practice_note: Medium for legal-AI real-world testing documentation.

summary: Member States must support SMEs, start-ups, deployers and relevant public authorities through priority sandbox access, tailored awareness and training, advice channels, participation in standardisation, and proportionate conformity-assessment fees.
quote: "Member States shall undertake the following actions:"
legal_practice_note: Medium for small legal-AI vendors and deployers seeking guidance, standardisation participation or reduced conformity-assessment burdens.

summary: The AI Office must provide standardised templates, maintain a single information platform, organise awareness campaigns, and evaluate and promote procurement best-practice convergence for AI systems.
quote: "The AI Office shall undertake the following actions:"
legal_practice_note: Medium for legal-AI operators using official templates, guidance and procurement practices.

summary: Eligible microenterprises may comply with certain Article 17 quality-management elements in a simplified manner, and the Commission must develop guidelines on the simplified elements without reducing protection or compliance needs.
quote: "Microenterprises within the meaning of Recommendation 2003/361/EC may comply with certain elements of the quality management system required by Article 17 of this Regulation in a simplified manner, provided that they do not have partner enterprises or linked enterprises within the meaning of that Recommendation. For that purpose, the Commission shall develop"
legal_practice_note: Medium for microenterprise legal-AI vendors subject to high-risk quality-management duties.

summary: The microenterprise simplification must not be interpreted as exempting operators from any other Regulation requirements or obligations, including listed high-risk and post-market obligations.
quote: "Paragraph 1 of this Article shall not be interpreted as exempting those operators from fulfilling any other requirements or obligations laid down in this Regulation, including those established in Articles 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 72 and 73."
legal_practice_note: Medium for small legal-AI vendors because simplification does not remove other duties.

summary: The Commission must develop Union expertise and capabilities in AI through the AI Office.
quote: "The Commission shall develop Union expertise and capabilities in the field of AI through the AI Office"
legal_practice_note: Governance row with indirect relevance to legal practice.

summary: Member States must facilitate the tasks entrusted to the AI Office under the Regulation.
quote: "Member States shall facilitate the tasks entrusted to the AI Office, as reflected in this Regulation"
legal_practice_note: Governance row with indirect relevance to legal practice.

summary: The AI Office must be allocated adequate resources to perform its duties and exercise its enforcement powers effectively, without prejudice to the budgetary procedure.
quote: "the AI Office shall be allocated adequate resources to effectively perform its duties and exercise its powers in relation to the enforcement of this Regulation"
legal_practice_note: Governance resource row with indirect relevance to legal practice.

summary: The Regulation establishes the European Artificial Intelligence Board.
quote: "A European Artificial Intelligence Board (the ‘Board’) is hereby established"
legal_practice_note: Governance row with indirect relevance to legal practice.

summary: The Board is composed of one representative per Member State, with the EDPS as observer and the AI Office attending without voting; other relevant authorities, bodies or experts may be invited case by case.
quote: "The Board shall be composed of one representative per Member State. The European Data Protection Supervisor shall participate as observer"
legal_practice_note: Governance composition row with indirect relevance to legal practice.

summary: Each Board representative must be designated by the Member State for a three-year term, renewable once.
quote: "Each representative shall be designated by their Member State for a period of three years, renewable once"
legal_practice_note: Governance appointment row with indirect relevance to legal practice.

summary: Member States must ensure their Board representatives have relevant competences and powers, act as single contact points where appropriate, and are empowered to facilitate national consistency and coordination for AI Act implementation.
quote: "Member States shall ensure that their representatives on the Board:"
legal_practice_note: Governance coordination row with indirect relevance to legal practice.

summary: The Member State representatives must adopt the Board’s rules of procedure by two-thirds majority, covering Chair selection, mandate, tasks, voting and organisation of Board and subgroup activities.
quote: "The designated representatives of the Member States shall adopt the Board’s rules of procedure by a two-thirds majority"
legal_practice_note: Governance procedure row with indirect relevance to legal practice.

summary: The Board must establish two standing subgroups for cooperation and exchange among market surveillance authorities and notifying authorities on market-surveillance and notified-body issues.
